title: The History of FIFA and EA Sports FC | From 1993 To The Big Split | Gaming History
description: The full history of the FIFA football games: FIFA International Soccer in 1993, real player names, women's national teams in FIFA 16, the end of the EA and FIFA licence in 2022 and the arrival of EA Sports FC 24.

sections.heading: A football series with two names
sections.script: Welcome back to the channel. Today we are going through the history of the FIFA video games, one of the biggest sports series ever made, and the story of how it changed its name. For almost thirty years, the football games from EA Sports carried the FIFA name on the box. Then, at the end of twenty twenty two, that partnership ended, and the series came back as EA Sports FC. We will start in nineteen ninety three with the very first game, look at how real players and three dimensional stadiums arrived, see the moment women's national teams joined the game, and finish with the split and what has happened since. Every date comes from Wikipedia and from news coverage of each release. Let us kick off.

sections.heading: The Christmas rush of nineteen ninety three
sections.script: The story begins in the early nineties, when football games on home consoles were plenty but none of them carried an official licence from FIFA, the body that runs world football. Electronic Arts, already famous for its Madden American football games, wanted a football game of its own. According to the history of the first game, a rival game from the company U S Gold was also in development, so EA decided to move fast and aimed for a Christmas nineteen ninety three release. That decision shaped everything. The team had a very short time to build a game, yet the result would launch a series that is still running more than three decades later, long after many of its early rivals disappeared.

sections.heading: FIFA International Soccer
sections.script: FIFA International Soccer came out in December nineteen ninety three for the Sega Mega Drive, which many people know as the Genesis. According to Wikipedia, it was the first football game with an official FIFA licence, and it was ported to other systems in nineteen ninety four. It let you play as national teams. Reports say it became a very big seller in the United Kingdom during the Christmas period. That success is why EA kept going. The idea was simple and powerful. Football fans around the world wanted to play as their own country, and a game with the official FIFA name felt like the real thing. The name on the box became the series' strongest selling point.

sections.heading: Real names and a three dimensional pitch
sections.script: The series kept improving through the mid nineties. FIFA Soccer ninety six, released in nineteen ninety five, is remembered for two big steps. First, it added real player names through a licence with FIFPro, the international players' union, so you were no longer controlling made up names. Second, it introduced what EA called a Virtual Stadium, which gave the game real time three dimensional stadiums on several platforms. A few years later, FIFA Road to World Cup ninety eight, released in November nineteen ninety seven, added a full World Cup qualifying mode with every national team. Each new release added something fans could see right away, and that steady habit of adding features became the pattern for the whole series.

sections.heading: The yearly release machine
sections.script: After the nineties, FIFA settled into a rhythm that fans know very well: a new game every September, with updated squads, new kits and a famous player on the cover. This yearly cycle turned the series into a huge business, and it also made it one of the most debated series in gaming, because each year people argued about whether the changes were big enough. Wikipedia reports that the series passed one hundred million copies sold by twenty ten, and that it was over three hundred million by twenty twenty one. Those totals come from publisher reporting and should be read as rough numbers, but they show the scale. Few series in any genre have sold that much by following a single, simple promise: this year's football, played your way.

sections.heading: Ultimate Team and the modern game
sections.script: Over time the way people play the series changed. Online play became central, and the card collecting mode called Ultimate Team grew into one of the most talked about parts of the game. In this mode, you build your own squad from player cards and take it into matches online. The mode is still a major feature, and press coverage of the new series confirms that Ultimate Team carried over into EA Sports FC. We will not guess at how many people play it, because EA does not publish one clean number we can trust. What we can say is that the series moved from being a simple football game on a cartridge to a year round online service, and that changed how EA and its players think about the series.

sections.heading: Women's national teams arrive in FIFA 16
sections.script: One of the most important moments in the series came with FIFA sixteen. In May twenty fifteen, timed with the Women's World Cup in Canada, EA announced that the game would include twelve women's national teams for the first time in the franchise's history. The teams were Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, England, France, Germany, Italy, Mexico, Spain, Sweden and the United States. The game launched in September twenty fifteen. EA used motion capture with four players from the United States women's national team, and the Guinness World Records lists FIFA sixteen as the first soccer video game to feature female players. At first the women's teams could only play against each other and were not in Ultimate Team. Even so, it was a big step.

sections.heading: The split announced in twenty twenty two
sections.script: Then came the biggest news in the history of the series. On the tenth of May, twenty twenty two, EA Sports and FIFA announced that their long licensing agreement would end on the thirty first of December, twenty twenty two, after a one year extension to allow the release of FIFA twenty three. News outlets described it as the end of a thirty year partnership that came apart when the two sides could not agree on a new licence. FIFA twenty three launched on the twenty seventh of September, twenty twenty two, and became the last EA Sports game to carry the FIFA name. It was a strange moment for fans, because a name they had seen on the box since nineteen ninety three was about to disappear.

sections.heading: EA Sports FC 24 begins a new chapter
sections.script: EA did not stop making football games. The series came back as EA Sports FC, and the first main game, EA Sports FC twenty four, was released on the twenty ninth of September, twenty twenty three, with a week of early access for people who bought the Ultimate Edition. The game kept its licences with leagues, clubs and players, which is where most of the real football feel comes from, even without the FIFA name on the box. Since the licence ended, the two names have gone separate ways, but the core idea from nineteen ninety three is still alive: pick your team and play the match. Football fans now simply find that idea under a new name.

sections.heading: What the history teaches us
sections.script: Looking back, the story of FIFA and EA Sports FC is really a story about licences. The first game worked because the official name made fans trust it. Real player names in nineteen ninety five made it feel more real, women's national teams in twenty fifteen made it more welcoming, and the split in twenty twenty two proved that the gameplay and the clubs matter as much as the badge on the box. Through all of it, the series kept coming back every autumn, because football fans love to play the sport they watch. Thirty years from a Mega Drive cartridge to an online service is a long way, and it is a good reminder of how much a simple idea can grow when it is polished every single year.

sections.heading: Your favourite football game
sections.script: That was the history of FIFA and EA Sports FC, from the first game in December nineteen ninety three to the new name in twenty twenty three. Now we want to hear from you. Which football game was the first one you ever played, and which year of FIFA or EA Sports FC do you remember best? Was it the early Mega Drive days, the nineties with real player names, or the modern online era? Tell us in the comments, because we read them. If you enjoyed this history, subscribe to the channel and turn on notifications, since we are going through many more franchises, from racing to shooters to role playing games. Thanks for watching, and we will see you in the next video.
